reuse.why: Adds a shared skipsWeekendOccurrences predicate and keeps getDateWithSkippedWeekend for the move case, but getUpcomingDates and schedule-template write their own skip loops/filters instead of reusing a shared skip-or-move function.

duplication.why: The weekday-search loop with a 1000 cap exists in firstWeekdayOccurrence, lastWeekdayOccurrence and again inline in getUpcomingDates, and the 'skip if daily, else move if skipWeekend' dispatch is written separately in getNextDate, getUpcomingDates and schedule-template.

placement.why: The predicate and occurrence helpers sit in shared/schedules.ts next to getNextDate, and frequency is added to the recur data in rule-utils; the per-site dispatch, though, lives in the server callers rather than the shared module.

scope.why: Only the weekend rule, its call sites, a test and a release note.

maintainability.why: The rule's predicate is in one place but how it is applied (skip vs move, search limits) has three hand-written variants that must be kept in step.

bypasses_abstraction.where: getUpcomingDates in server/schedules/app.ts iterates occurrences and filters weekends itself instead of using the new firstWeekdayOccurrence/getNextDate path; schedule-template re-derives skip vs move around getDateWithSkippedWeekend.

disguised_duplication.where: The inline loop in getUpcomingDates is firstWeekdayOccurrence reshaped to collect several dates; schedule-template's resolveDate/isSkippedOccurrence restates getNextDate's skip-vs-move branch under new names.

one_place.where: Only the 'is this a skipping schedule' predicate (skipsWeekendOccurrences) is shared; the skip-vs-move application is decided separately in shared/schedules.ts getNextDate, server/schedules/app.ts getUpcomingDates and server/budget/schedule-template.ts.
